title: Install rules and relocatable packages
summary: Install a library with GNUInstallDirs, separate build and install include paths, and export a target set.

scenario.briefing: The metrics library installs into an absolute /usr/local path and publishes no targets, so another project cannot find it. Install with GNUInstallDirs and export the library.

objectives.description: Install targets and headers with relocatable destinations.
Identify install rules that break package consumers.
Explain what find_package needs beyond a targets file.

hints: The build tree and the install tree need different include paths.
Use install(TARGETS ... EXPORT ...) for the library.

misconceptions.description: Installing to /usr/local/lib instead of a GNUInstallDirs destination.
misconceptions.feedback: An absolute destination ignores the prefix and breaks packaging. Use CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR and CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR.

misconceptions.description: Publishing the source include path to installed consumers.
misconceptions.testDescription: The target's include path differs between build and install.
misconceptions.feedback: A consumer sees the installed tree. Guard source paths with BUILD_INTERFACE and installed paths with INSTALL_INTERFACE.

misconceptions.description: Installing the archive without an export set.
misconceptions.testDescription: The export set is installed for find_package consumers.
misconceptions.feedback: install(TARGETS) copies files. The EXPORT set and install(EXPORT) create the imported target definitions a consumer needs.

misconceptions.description: Believing a static library cannot be exported.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Approving the claim that static libraries cannot be installed or exported.
misconceptions.feedback: Static libraries have usage requirements too. The export carries include directories, definitions, and link dependencies.

misconceptions.description: Expecting find_package to read a targets file directly.
misconceptions.feedback: find_package in CONFIG mode looks for a package config file, which includes the targets file and defines the package.

sections.title: Install rules describe a tree
sections.body: GNUInstallDirs defines standard destinations such as CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR and CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR. install(TARGETS) copies the binary into that tree, and install(DIRECTORY) copies headers. Absolute destinations bypass the configured prefix and make packaging hostile.

sections.title: Usage requirements change between trees
sections.body: While building, a consumer needs the source include directory. After installation, it needs the installed include directory. $<BUILD_INTERFACE:...> and $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:...> keep the two paths separate in one target definition.

sections.title: A package is a config file plus targets
sections.body: install(TARGETS ... EXPORT ...) records the library in an export set. install(EXPORT ...) writes the imported target definitions. find_package(campus_metrics CONFIG) looks for campus_metricsConfig.cmake, which includes that targets file and often checks the version.

steps.title: Install and export the library
steps.prompt: Edit CMakeLists.txt. Install metrics into GNUInstallDirs destinations, add the install include path, install the headers, and export the target set with a namespace.
hints: Install the headers and the export set.

files.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(campus_metrics LANGUAGES CXX)

include(GNUInstallDirs)

add_library(metrics STATIC src/metrics.cpp)
target_include_directories(metrics PUBLIC
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>)

# TODO: install the library, headers, and an export set
install(TARGETS metrics DESTINATION /usr/local/lib)

steps.title: Review the install rules
steps.prompt: Review the build file and select every real problem.
hints: Check the destination paths and the published include directory.
An absolute destination ignores the install prefix.
A source path in an installed interface points at a tree the consumer does not have.
An archive without an export cannot be imported by find_package.

artifact.title: CMakeLists.txt
artifact.caption: The library installs to an absolute path, publishes its source include directory, and has no export set.
artifact.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(campus_metrics LANGUAGES CXX)

add_library(metrics STATIC src/metrics.cpp)
target_include_directories(metrics PUBLIC /home/ada/campus/include)

install(TARGETS metrics DESTINATION /usr/local/lib)

findings.label: The install destination is the absolute path /usr/local/lib.
Installed consumers receive the source include path /home/ada/campus/include.
The library is installed without an export set or imported target.
A static library cannot be installed or exported.
Headers must be installed into the bin directory.

verdicts.label: Block the install rules until the paths and export are fixed.
Ship it; absolute paths are acceptable for a library.
Only formatting and naming need work.

steps.explanation: Absolute destinations and source include paths bind the package to one machine. Without an export set, another project has no imported target to link. Use GNUInstallDirs, BUILD_INTERFACE/INSTALL_INTERFACE, and install(EXPORT ...).

steps.title: Transfer to a package config
steps.prompt: A consumer runs find_package(campus_metrics CONFIG REQUIRED), but the install contains only campus_metricsTargets.cmake. What is missing?
hints: CONFIG mode looks for a package config file.
The targets file defines imported targets but is not the entry point.
The config file includes the targets file.
A version file and a config file make the package discoverable.

quiz.prompt: A consumer runs find_package(campus_metrics CONFIG REQUIRED), but the install contains only campus_metricsTargets.cmake. What is missing?

options.label: A campus_metricsConfig.cmake that includes the targets file.
Nothing; find_package reads the targets file directly.
A second copy of the library under a different name.
The consumer must point CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH at the original source tree.

quiz.explanation: find_package in CONFIG mode searches for a package config file. That file defines the package and includes the exported targets. The targets file alone is not the documented entry point.
